SMTO-CFG-0087 — This Task isn't allowed to turn on that Skill

GUID: 56248619-40e7-5d2b-8fb5-207e26366ab0
Slug: capability-activation-outside-ceiling
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: capability_activation

What happened

  • The Skill the Agent wanted is outside what this Task was allowed to use when it started. SMTO didn't turn it on, and the Task can only go on with the Skills it already has.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check whether the Task keeps going with other tools. If its result is good enough, you don't need to do anything. The Agent is told to carry on with the Skills this Task is allowed to use.
  2. If you want the Skill used, open Capabilities by the message box and make sure it isn't set to Never or − Exclude. A Skill blocked in your capability choices stays outside what new Tasks may use.
  3. If the Agent mode menu by the message box says Ask, switch it to Agent. Ask mode only gives advice, so Skills that change things are outside what it may use.
  4. Check what the Task already finished, then send a new request for the rest. A new request starts with your current settings, while a running Task keeps the ones it started with.

What success looks like

  • The new Task uses the Skill without this message.

If it still fails

  • Send Copy error details to the person who manages SMTO; a Workflow or Gateway limit may be keeping this Skill out. Don't try to switch off Permissions or other safety checks to get around it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Activation was refused because the requested Skill lies outside the run's accepted capability ceiling (capability_activation.outside_ceiling); this retained label has no direct current classification branch.

What this means

  • This retained outside-ceiling kind has no direct current classification branch; current activation checks accepted ceilings, prospective grants and hard upstream restrictions. The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.

Why this can happen

  • This retained outside-ceiling kind has no direct current classification branch; current activation checks accepted ceilings, prospective grants and hard upstream restrictions.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect actual activation classification and grantability; this retained label does not establish whether a supported human grant could apply.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the actual activation result (classify and prospective in src/agent_runtime/native/capability_activation.py) together with the run's capability_ceiling and grant_provenance.hard_tool_ids. Use the supported grant path where one is offered, or change the user capability policy, agent mode or upstream workflow or Gateway restriction for a new run; never widen the existing run's accepted ceiling.
  • Use the current activation result's supported policy/grant path, or continue with permitted alternatives; do not bypass the accepted ceiling.

Retry and execution caution

  • The reported capability or interaction condition changes.

How to verify the fix

  • Only authority accepted through existing policy/grant controls can activate the capability.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass frozen authority, operation permissions or credential requirements.

Technical notes

  • The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
